title: Sparks star Nneka Ogwumike ends WNBA 30th anniversary game with stunning buzzer-beater
content:
LOS ANGELES — Nneka Ogwumike couldn’t fight back the tears as the ESPN broadcast asked her what it meant to have a celebration of the WNBA’s evolution on her home court.

No. 30 hit the game-winner at the buzzer for the Los Angeles Sparks’ 98-97 victory over the New York Liberty on Sunday night to commemorate the league’s 30th season and honor all of the legends in the building who helped the franchise survive to this point. It was all too much for the 15-year veteran to process during her live interview minutes after the victory. Thus, the overflow of emotion.

“What a great moment, and the perfect person to hit that,” Los Angeles coach Lynne Roberts said.

The passage of time was omnipresent for the Sparks and Liberty. Lisa Leslie and Kym Hampton lined up at center court for the pregame tip-off, just as they did for the WNBA’s debut game on this date in 1997. Los Angeles legends DeLisha Milton-Jones and Tamecka Dixon were at Sparks practice on Saturday, and the New York Liberty welcomed original roster members Sue Wicks, Hampton, Teresa Weatherspoon and Vickie Johnson at their walk-through.

The history and the present of the league all intertwined Sunday, and Ogwumike — the fourth-leading scorer in WNBA history and the architect of the last two collective bargaining agreements as the players’ union president — tied it all together.

With L.A. down two and without a timeout, the Sparks went to an action they were familiar with, and when the Liberty helped off the wing, Erica Wheeler found Ogwumike for the 3-pointer and a piece of history.

“Who better to make the game-winning shot? It’s Nneka. She’s awesome,” Wheeler said on the postgame broadcast. “We had to get this win for our alumni, this 30 years. The crowd was amazing. It was too much going on for us to not get this win.”

Sabrina Ionescu returned to the Liberty’s lineup last week after missing seven games due to back soreness. But since her return, she’s navigated inconsistencies.

She finished with just 5 points against the Washington Mystics in her first game back on June 14. Three nights later, she scored 10, including a game-winning layup in the Liberty’s 96-95 win over the Sky on the road. Against the Mystics on June 19, she recorded 9 points and three assists.

The Liberty have had very little time this season with a clean injury report. When Ionescu returned to the rotation, she talked about needing to reestablish chemistry with her team. Against the Sparks, she looked like she was still searching for her rhythm. She finished with just 2 points, two assists and three rebounds in 22 minutes. Most notable was Liberty coach Chris DeMarco leaving her on the bench in the closing minutes as the Sparks mounted their comeback. Instead, he opted for rookie guard Pauline Astier alongside Breanna Stewart, Jonquel Jones, Satou Sabally and Leonie Fiebich.

Astier poured in 17 points off the bench. Stewart had 16 points, nine rebounds and four assists. Sabally finished with 14 points, and Jones led the way with 18 points, eight rebounds and three assists.

DeMarco is still tinkering with lineups. He opted to move Marine Johannes to the bench in favor of starting Sabally against the Sparks to give the Liberty a stronger defensive option alongside Ionescu. It’s likely DeMarco will continue to be flexible with his starting five.
